newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain sets measures to foster steady job contracts.
newsitem.headline: Spain sets measures to foster steady job contracts.

text.p: Spain, which earlier on Friday approved a labour reform law, has also unveiled measures designed to encourage the use of the new permanent contracts, a statement said.

The Labour Ministry explained that new hiring will cost a firm 40 percent less in total social security costs, while transforming temporary contracts into permanent ones will cost just 50 percent of the current total.
The statement added that for workers aged 45 or older, the new contract will be discounted by 60 percent in the first two years and by 50 percent thereafter.
Firms will get a 60 percent social security discount in the first two years if they hire women in a business area with an overrepresentation of male workers.
Contracts for the long-term unemployed and workers under 30 will be offered a 40 percent discount.
To change temporary, training, or new contracts to replace early retirements into permanent ones would be discounted by 50 percent.
The statement did not make clear how long the incentives would be maintained.
